chunks: And from him, from Hanan who said,

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Indeed Al-Husayn ibn Al-Munzar narrated from you that you said: The slaughter is [valid] by the Naming, and it is not trusted upon except for its rightful ones.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'They have introduced something in it which I do not desire.' Hanan said, 'So I asked a Christian, and I said to him, 'What do you say when you slaughter?' So he said, 'We say, 'In the name of the Messiah'.

key_terms.أَهْلَهَا: Its rightful ones (People of the Book)
key_terms.بِاسْمِ الْمَسِيحِ: In the name of the Messiah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on slaughter by the People of the Book if they say 'In the name of the Messiah'?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that while the People of the Book perform slaughter by invoking a name, the specific name used by Christians ('the Messiah') is not the one desired for valid consumption, indicating a nuance in the 'Naming' condition. This hadith highlights the Shia scholarly distinction between the general act of naming and the specific theological appropriateness of the name invoked, as confirmed by Hanan’s inquiry with a Christian. It underscores the importance of verifying the actual practice of the People of the Book rather than assuming uniformity in their ritual slaughter.
